form_cues: Pull the chin level with the working hand.
en.description: Archer Pull Up pulls toward one hand while the other arm stays straight, shifting most of the load to the working side.
en.safety_note: Work up from wide-grip pull ups and stop if the shoulders or elbows feel strain on the stretched side.
instructions: Hang from a wide overhand grip with your arms fully extended.
Pull toward your right hand while the left arm stays straight out to the side.
Lower to a full hang, then pull toward your left hand with the right arm straight.
Alternate sides for the planned repetitions.
common_mistakes: Twisting the torso to cheat the pull.
Dropping fast on the way down.

form_cues: Lower the chest past the working hand.
en.description: Archer Push Up lowers toward one hand while the other arm stays straight, loading one side at a time.
en.safety_note: Raise the hands on a bench if the shoulders cannot control the descent.
instructions: Start in a push up position with the hands set wider than the shoulders.
Bend one elbow to lower the chest toward that hand while the other arm stays straight out to the side.
Press back to the start, then repeat toward the other hand.
Alternate sides for the planned repetitions.

form_cues: Track the knee over the toes.
en.description: Bulgarian Split Squat (Bodyweight) bends the hips and knees through a rear-foot-elevated squat path with no added load.
en.safety_note: Choose a depth and a stance that keep the foot, knee, and spine stable.
instructions: Place the top of one foot on a bench behind you and stand on the other leg with your arms folded or at your sides.
Bend both knees until the front thigh approaches parallel while the front heel stays planted.
Pause without letting the front knee collapse inward.
Drive through the front foot to stand, then switch sides after the set.

form_cues: Lean back slightly to bring the chest to the bar.
Drive the elbows toward the hips.
Pull the shoulders down at the top.
en.description: Chest to Bar Pull Up pulls from a dead hang until the chest touches the bar, a higher pull than a standard pull up.
en.safety_note: Build a solid pull up first and stop if the shoulders or elbows pinch at the top.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip and your arms fully extended.
Brace the core and drive the elbows down and back as you pull.
Keep pulling until the chest touches the bar.
Lower to a full hang under control before the next repetition.
common_mistakes: Stopping with the chin at the bar.

form_cues: Look slightly ahead of the hands.
en.description: Crow Pose balances the body on the hands with the knees resting on the upper arms and the feet off the floor.
en.safety_note: Place a folded mat in front of the hands and start with a gentle lean forward.
instructions: Squat with your hands flat on the floor shoulder-width apart and your knees wide.
Rest your knees on the backs of your upper arms and lean the weight forward over the hands.
Lift one foot, then the other, and hold with the core braced for the planned number of seconds.
Lower the feet to the floor to end the hold.
common_mistakes: Letting the knees slip off the arms.

form_cues: Keep the hips in line with the torso.
en.description: Dragon Flag (Negative) lowers the straight body slowly from the top of a dragon flag while resisting the arch in the lower back.
en.safety_note: Use a tucked or shortened range until the body can lower as one unit.
instructions: Lie on a bench, grip the edge behind your head, and raise the hips and legs into one straight line.
Brace the core and lower the body as one unit as slowly as you can control.
Stop before the hips drop or the back arches.
Bend the knees to return to the top, then reset.
common_mistakes: Dropping fast through the last part.

form_cues: Pull hard from the first inch.
en.description: Explosive Pull Up accelerates hard from a hang to bring the chest high toward the bar, then lowers under control.
en.safety_note: Build strict pull up strength first and stop when the speed of the pull starts to fade.
instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip and your arms fully extended.
Brace the core and set the shoulders down.
Pull as fast as you can, driving the elbows down until the chest reaches the bar.
Lower slowly to a full hang before the next repetition.
common_mistakes: Starting the next rep from bent arms.

form_cues: Keep the chin above the bar.
en.description: Flexed-Arm Hang holds the chin above a pull-up bar with the elbows bent for as many seconds as you can keep the position.
en.safety_note: Use a stable step to reach the top position and step down when the grip fades.
instructions: Use a step or jump to start with your chin above a secure pull-up bar and an overhand grip.
Set the shoulders down and brace the core.
Hold the chin above the bar with the elbows bent for the planned number of seconds.
Step down to end the hold rather than dropping.
common_mistakes: Letting the chin sink below the bar.

form_cues: Keep the thighs in line with the torso.
en.description: Front Lever Hold (Advanced Tuck) holds the body horizontal with the back flat and the hips open, a longer lever than the tuck.
en.safety_note: Move up from the tuck only when you can hold it with a flat back, and lower before the form breaks.
instructions: Hang from a secure bar with an overhand grip and your arms straight.
Pull the shoulders down and lift the hips until the back is flat and parallel to the floor.
Open the hips so the thighs line up with the torso and keep the knees bent.
Hold for the planned number of seconds, then tuck and lower to a hang.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to hold longer.

form_cues: Keep the extended leg in line with the torso.
en.description: Front Lever Hold (One Leg) holds the body horizontal with one leg extended straight and the other knee tucked.
en.safety_note: Alternate the extended leg across sets and lower out of the hold before the grip or form fails.
instructions: Hang from a secure bar with an overhand grip and your arms straight.
Pull the shoulders down and lift into a flat horizontal back with the knees tucked.
Extend one leg straight, keep the other knee tucked, and hold for the planned number of seconds.
Tuck the leg back in and lower to a hang, then switch legs on the next set.
common_mistakes: Tilting the hips to one side.

form_cues: Keep the hips in line with the shoulders.
en.description: Front Lever Hold (Straddle) holds the body horizontal with both legs extended and spread wide to shorten the lever.
en.safety_note: Spread the legs wider if the hips drop, and lower before the shoulders or elbows lose control.
instructions: Hang from a secure bar with an overhand grip and your arms straight.
Pull the shoulders down and raise the body until it is flat and parallel to the floor.
Extend both legs straight out and spread them as wide as needed to hold the line.
Hold for the planned number of seconds, then tuck the knees and lower to a hang.

en.description: Front Lever Hold (Tuck) holds the body horizontal under a bar with the knees pulled tightly to the chest.
en.safety_note: Build up from hangs and rows, and lower out of the hold before the grip or shoulders give out.
instructions: Hang from a secure bar with an overhand grip and your arms straight.
Pull the shoulders down and lift the hips until the back is parallel to the floor.
Tuck the knees tightly to the chest and hold for the planned number of seconds.
Lower to a hang with control to end the hold.

form_cues: Keep the body in a straight line.
en.description: Handstand Hold (Chest to Wall) holds an upside-down line on straight arms with the chest facing the wall for a set number of seconds.
en.safety_note: Practice on a clear floor and come down by walking the feet back before the arms tire.
instructions: Set your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart, a short step from the wall.
Walk the feet up the wall until the body forms a straight line with the chest facing the wall.
Push tall through the shoulders and brace the trunk.
Hold for the planned number of seconds, then walk the feet down one step at a time.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back toward the wall.

form_cues: Stack the shoulders over the wrists.
en.description: Handstand Push Up (Negative) lowers slowly from a wall-supported handstand until the head nears the floor.
en.safety_note: Use a wall or spotter and stop before the head or shoulders land uncontrollably.
instructions: Kick up into a handstand against a wall with the arms straight and the trunk braced.
Bend the elbows to lower the head toward the floor as slowly as you can control.
Stop before the head touches the floor.
Walk the feet down and reset between repetitions.
common_mistakes: Dropping fast through the last half.

form_cues: Keep the lower back on the floor.
en.description: Hollow Body Hold presses the lower back down while the shoulders and legs lift into a shallow curve for a set number of seconds.
en.safety_note: Bend the knees or bring the arms to the sides if the lower back lifts off the floor.
instructions: Lie on your back with the legs together and the arms extended overhead.
Press the lower back into the floor and brace the abdominals.
Lift the shoulders and the heels a few inches and hold the curve for the planned number of seconds.
Lower to the floor with control to end the hold.
common_mistakes: Bending the knees to hold the shape.

form_cues: Keep the body in one straight line.
Squeeze the shoulder blades at the top.
en.description: With the feet raised on a bench or box, pull the chest to a fixed bar while the body stays in a straight line.
en.safety_note: Check that the bar and the bench are stable, and lower the feet if the body cannot hold a straight line.
instructions: Set a bar at about waist height and lie under it with your heels on a bench or box.
Grip the bar with an overhand grip and straighten the body from shoulders to heels.
Pull the chest toward the bar by driving the elbows back.
Pause, then lower until the arms are straight without losing the line.

form_cues: Pull the knees toward the chest.
en.description: L-Sit Hold (Tuck) supports the body on the hands with the knees pulled in and lifted off the floor for a set number of seconds.
en.safety_note: Use a flat, clear surface and stop when the wrists or shoulders lose stable support.
instructions: Sit on the floor, or between parallettes, with your hands beside the hips.
Press down through the hands and lift the hips and feet off the floor.
Pull the knees toward the chest and hold the tuck for the planned number of seconds.
Lower to the floor with control to end the hold.

form_cues: Pull the bar toward the lower chest.
Keep the bar close through the transition.
Use a lighter band as you get stronger.
en.description: Muscle Up (Band) uses a resistance band looped over the bar to help pull from a hang over the bar and press to support.
en.safety_note: Check the band and its anchor before hanging, and pick a band that lets you control the descent.
instructions: Loop a resistance band over the bar and secure it, then step a foot or knee into the loop.
Hang with an overhand grip and pull the chest explosively toward the bar.
Lean the chest over the bar through the transition and press to straight arms.
Lower under control to a full hang, then repeat.
common_mistakes: Bouncing out of the band to skip the pull.
Pressing before the chest is over the bar.

form_cues: Keep the bar close to the body.
Take at least three seconds to lower.
en.description: Muscle Up (Negative) starts in support above the bar and lowers slowly through the transition to a full hang.
en.safety_note: Use a box or stable step to reach the top and stop if the shoulders or elbows lose control of the descent.
instructions: Use a box or jump to start in support above the bar with your arms straight.
Lean the chest over the bar and begin to bend the elbows.
Lower slowly through the transition, keeping the bar close to the chest.
Continue down to a full hang, then step down and reset.
common_mistakes: Letting the bar drift away from the chest.

en.description: Parallel Bar Support Hold holds the body above parallel bars on straight arms for a set number of seconds.
en.safety_note: Make sure the bars are stable and step down when the shoulders or wrists start to give.
instructions: Grip parallel bars and jump or step up to support the body on straight arms.
Press the shoulders down away from the ears and lock the elbows.
Hold the body still with the legs together for the planned number of seconds.
Step down or lower with control to end the hold.
common_mistakes: Letting the chest sink between the arms.

form_cues: Move the head between the hands.
en.description: Pike Pushup (Feet Elevated) presses from an inverted V with the feet on a box, so the shoulders carry more of the load.
en.safety_note: Start with a low box and stop if the shoulders or wrists cannot control the descent.
instructions: Place your feet on a bench or box and your hands on the floor shoulder-width apart with the hips high.
Brace the core and bend the elbows to lower the head toward the floor between the hands.
Press through the palms to straighten the arms and return to the pike.
Keep the hips high through every repetition.

form_cues: Squeeze the glutes and the abdominals.
en.description: Pseudo Planche Lean holds a plank with the shoulders shifted forward past the hands for a set number of seconds.
en.safety_note: Warm up the wrists first and lean only as far as the wrists and shoulders feel steady.
instructions: Start in a push up position with the hands turned out beside the hips.
Lean forward until the shoulders are past the wrists and the weight sits over the hands.
Hold the lean with straight arms for the planned number of seconds.
Rock back to the start to end the hold.

form_cues: Hold the lean through the whole rep.
Keep the body in a straight line.
en.description: Pseudo Planche Push Up shifts the shoulders forward over the hands so the push up loads the front of the shoulders and chest harder.
en.safety_note: Warm up the wrists first and lean only as far as the wrists and shoulders feel steady.
instructions: Start in a push up position with the hands turned out and set beside the hips.
Lean forward until the shoulders are well past the wrists.
Lower the chest with the elbows close to the ribs.
Press up to straight arms while holding the lean.
common_mistakes: Rocking back to the start position.

form_cues: Track the knee over the toes.
en.description: Shrimp Squat lowers on one leg while the other knee bends behind you, then drives back to standing.
en.safety_note: Lower to a folded mat and use a wall or rail for balance until the movement is under control.
instructions: Stand on one leg and bend the other knee, holding the foot behind you with the same-side hand.
Lower slowly on the standing leg until the back knee touches the floor lightly.
Keep the front heel planted and the torso tall.
Press through the standing foot to return to standing, then switch legs after the set.

en.description: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift (Bodyweight) hinges on one leg while the free leg reaches back, then stands tall and switches.
en.safety_note: Keep a soft bend in the standing knee and hold a wall or rail if balance is the limit.
instructions: Stand on one foot with a slight bend in the knee and your arms hanging in front of you.
Hinge at the hips as the free leg reaches straight back.
Lower the torso until it is close to parallel to the floor with the back flat.
Squeeze the glute to stand tall, then switch legs after the set.
common_mistakes: Bending the standing knee into a squat.

form_cues: Move slowly through the shoulder rotation.
Keep the knees tucked until past the arms.
Stay in control at the deepest point.
en.description: Skin the Cat tucks the legs through the arms from a hang, rolls into a deep shoulder stretch, then reverses back to a hang.
en.safety_note: Use a low bar so your feet can reach the floor, and stop if the shoulders feel strain at the deepest point.
instructions: Hang from a secure bar or rings with your arms straight.
Tuck the knees up and pull the hips over toward the bar.
Pass the feet through the arms and lower the legs toward the floor as the shoulders rotate.
Reverse the path slowly to return to the hang.
common_mistakes: Letting go of the bar early.

form_cues: Keep the bar close to the body.
Press the shoulders down at the top.
en.description: Straight Bar Dip supports the body over a single straight bar, then lowers the chest and presses back up to straight arms.
en.safety_note: Make sure the bar is fixed and set at hip height, and stop if the shoulders or wrists lose stable support.
instructions: Grip a straight bar at about hip height and press up to support with the elbows straight.
Lean the torso forward and bend the elbows to lower the chest toward the bar.
Stop when the bar is near the lower chest and the shoulders stay stable.
Press back up to straight arms.
common_mistakes: Letting the bar drift away from the body.

en.description: Triceps Dip (Negative) lowers slowly from the top of a parallel-bar dip, then steps back up to reset.
en.safety_note: Step or jump to the top instead of pressing up, and stop when the shoulders lose control of the descent.
instructions: Jump or step up to support on parallel bars with the elbows straight and the shoulders down.
Keep the torso slightly forward and bend the elbows to lower as slowly as you can control.
Stop when the upper arms approach parallel to the floor.
Step down, return to the top, and repeat.
